textbook: Clean cutaway textbook illustration of a SINGLE MITOCHONDRION — an ORGANELLE inside a eukaryotic cell, NOT a cell and NOT a bacterium — centred in a square 1:1 1080x1080 frame with generous negative space around the structure so labels can attach later. Fill the whole square edge-to-edge on a neutral dark-charcoal cytosol background with NO border, frame, vignette or letterbox. Match the exact house look of a refined educational plate: a MUTED, slightly desaturated palette (soft dusty tints, never bright primary or cartoon colours), THIN clean outlines (not heavy black strokes), gentle soft shading, each structure its own distinct soft colour fill. STRUCTURE: an elongated bean/sausage-shaped organelle shown in cutaway. The OUTER MEMBRANE is a single, perfectly SMOOTH, unbroken steel-blue line forming the outer boundary — absolutely no folds in it. Just inside, separated by a thin pale-blue INTERMEMBRANE SPACE that runs continuously all the way around, sits a second, separate INNER MEMBRANE in warm brick-red. This inner membrane is thrown into many DEEP, closely-spaced TRANSVERSE FOLDS — the CRISTAE — that cross most of the width of the organelle. Every single crista must clearly connect back to the inner membrane at a narrow neck (a crista junction) on BOTH sides where it meets the boundary membrane — cristae are folds OF the inner membrane, and must NEVER appear as separate free-floating shelves, plates or islands disconnected from it. The cristae project INTO a warm cream-tan MATRIX that completely fills the space between and around them — the matrix must read as fully ENCLOSED by the inner membrane, never open, never breached, never leaking outside the organelle. In the matrix, draw one small tangled GOLDEN-YELLOW RING — the mitochondrial DNA, clearly circular, never a straight line or an X-shape — plus a scatter of small slate-grey granules (mitoribosomes) near it, and a few tiny soft-green mushroom-shaped knobs (ATP synthase particles, a round head on a short stalk) dotting the matrix-facing surface of several cristae. CRITICAL SCIENTIFIC RULES: exactly TWO membranes, never one; the cristae are CONNECTED to the inner membrane at both ends, never floating loose pieces inside the matrix; the matrix is a single closed compartment, never open to the outside; the mtDNA is a small closed CIRCLE, never linear or branched; do NOT draw a nucleus (no double envelope with pores, no nucleolus, no chromatin) anywhere inside it; do NOT draw a bacterial cell wall, capsule, flagellum or pili; do NOT draw stacked green thylakoid discs (that is a chloroplast, a different organelle). Exactly ONE mitochondrion in the picture, no duplicates. Absolutely NO text, letters, numbers, labels, scale bars, arrows or watermarks in the image.
sem: Photorealistic false-color scanning electron micrograph of a SINGLE MITOCHONDRION, freeze-fractured to reveal its internal folded membrane architecture in cutaway — in the manner of classic organelle electron microscopy — centred in a square 1:1 1080x1080 frame with generous empty margin. Fill the whole square edge-to-edge with NO border, frame, vignette or letterbox. Subject: an elongated bean-shaped organelle with true 3D surface relief. A smooth, unbroken OUTER MEMBRANE (cool steel-blue false colour) wraps the whole structure with no folds in it whatsoever; fractured open to reveal the interior, a separate INNER MEMBRANE (warm brick-red false colour) is visible thrown into many deep parallel transverse folds — the CRISTAE — each one clearly continuous with the inner membrane, never a detached free-floating shelf. The cristae project into a densely granular cream-tan MATRIX filling the fully enclosed interior; nestled in the matrix, a small tangled golden-yellow ring of mitochondrial DNA sits near a scatter of tiny slate-grey granular mitoribosomes, and tiny pale-green stalked knobs (ATP synthase particles) stud the matrix-facing surface of the cristae folds. Shallow depth of field so the far background falls softly out of focus, cool studio microscopy lighting. Do NOT show a single unfolded membrane, a nucleus with pores, a bacterial cell wall or flagellum, or stacked green thylakoid discs. Do NOT draw the cristae as separate loose plates disconnected from the inner membrane. Single mitochondrion only, no duplicates. Absolutely NO text, letters, numbers, labels, scale bars, arrows or watermarks anywhere in the image.
